source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Routine screening being generally recommended for essentially every asymptomatic adult, regardless of their own individual risk factor profile","B":"Screening is not generally recommended for asymptomatic, average-risk adults, given limited evidence of benefit and potential for harm from unnecessary intervention","C":"No screening test of any kind actually existing today for detecting carotid artery stenosis in an asymptomatic client at a routine visit","D":"Screening being recommended mainly for clients under age 40, rather than for the older, higher-risk adults who are more typically affected"}}
source_row.rationale: Current guidance generally does not recommend routine carotid artery stenosis screening for asymptomatic, average-risk adults, given limited evidence of overall benefit and potential for harm from unnecessary intervention.
source_row.source_name: USPSTF — Carotid Artery Stenosis Screening Recommendations
